correctness.rationale: By half-normal Gaussian direction representation the spherical centroid is proportional to (1,...,1). In d=3 all normals perpendicular to centroid reduce by permutations and sign reversal to (a,1-a,-1), a in [0,1], with boundary zero normal giving 1/2. The complementary spherical triangle has rays (0,0,1),(1,0,a),(0,1,1-a), and solid-angle formula yields P=1-(4/pi)atan[(sqrt(1+a²)-a)(sqrt(1+(1-a)²)-(1-a))]. Independently the spherical-coordinate integral is (2/pi)∫q/sqrt(1+q²), whose second derivative is strictly negative; symmetry gives unique maximum at a=1/2 and exact minimum by normal reversal. For all d, H_d≤mean(H1..H_{d-1}) gives E erf(mean/√2), strictly rising by leave-one-out sample means and strict Jensen concavity, converging by SLLN. Independent quadrature agreed at six parameters; exact minimum 0.46455905439754 and canonical limit erf(1/√pi). The d>=4 assertion is confined to specified normals.
residual_risks: Global optimization is proven only for d=3, not higher dimensional normals.
